children: The initial public offering (IPO) of Mahanadi Coalfields (MCL), the largest subsidiary of Coal India,  will be open till November 23. The coal mining company, which produces 21 per cent of India’s overall domestic coal,  accounts for 28 per cent of Coal India’s production. The IPO is an offer for sale raising ₹9,001 crore for its parent Coal India, which will divest 10 per cent through the IPO. At the upper end of the IPO price band, the company is priced at 9 times annualised H1FY27 earnings.

The relatively lower valuation accounts for the lack of growth of the company, which reported revenue and PAT decline of 1.7 per cent/5 per cent CAGR in FY24-26. With improving demand for thermal power and hence coal, volume growth can recover. But more importantly, the company also reported a significant 8-9 per cent dividend yield and is likely to sustain the same with a 70 per cent plus payout ratio. Considering the dividend yield,  yield-seeking investors can consider the IPO for the long term.

MCL operates 17 mines across Talcher and IB valley in Odisha, mining non-coking coal  used in power generation. Its main customers include power companies (72 per cent by volume in H1FY27), captive power plants and other smaller industries (13 per cent each).
As per the RHP, MCL mines have a lifespan of 45 years: assuming volume growth at 4.7 per cent CAGR (FY16-26 rate of sales growth) and applying a historical conversion rate of resource to reserves.

First, realisations from sales are based on notified pricing mechanism administered by Coal India, which are intended to ensure reliable and affordable coal to State-run power companies. The other two segments rely on market dynamics and provide 15-30 per cent higher realisations, as shown in the figure.

In H1FY27, blended realisation of ₹1,447 per tonne has declined at a 3.7 per cent CAGR from FY24, while international coal prices were flat during the period. Indonesian coal, which stands at ₹5,543 per tonne, and Coal India realisations were at a 56 per cent premium in FY26 at ₹2,265 per tonne. Grade differences can explain a part of the gap, as MCL grades are lower than the two.
MCL may consider a renewed pricing  strategy as it transitions to a listed entity after the IPO.

The sales volume has grown at 2.9 per cent CAGR in FY24-26 and risen  8 per cent in H1FY27 compared to the 4.7 per cent CAGR in FY16-26. The MCL management noted the coal destocking at thermal power plants and lower power generation last year, attributing  delayed monsoons as the reason for low growth. The company expects strong volume growth this fiscal year due to a drier monsoon (low hydro power contribution) and growth in demand for thermal power.

Over a long term, coal demand will face decelerating demand growth, as India aspires for 50 per cent power capacity from renewable sources by 2030. But even at this pace, India needs 80 GW of thermal power by 2031-32 compared to 228-GW thermal capacity currently,  and coal demand should increase from around 1,000 mtpa in FY25 to 1,600 mtpa by FY31. MCL, being the leading and lowest cost provider with sufficient environmental clearance for mining, should benefit from the increased demand.

MCL has relatively-higher EBITDA margins in the industry at 40 per cent in H1FY27 compared to Coal India (23.3 per cent), NMDC (32.8 per cent), or international coal peers in the 17-19 per cent range. This is primarily owing to the rich asset base in Talcher and IB valley in Odisha.

The high profitability is owing to opencast mining at shallow depths. Around 99.85 per cent of MCL coal production in FY26 is from open cast mining, which does not involve mining deep into earth for resource extraction — a costly operation. Surface mining technology is employed for these resources, further lowering costs. The opencast mines have around 80 per cent of resources at a depth of less than 300 metres, which sustains the company’s margin profile. But owing to flat volume growth, EBITDA margins have declined from 46 per cent in FY24 and may recover with improving volumes.

MCL reported an average 36 per cent PAT margin in FY24-26, of which an average 76 per cent was distributed as dividends in the period which supports the average 9.4 per cent dividend yield in the period (dividend amount divided by IPO implied market-cap). It is likely to sustain the payout ratio, as evidenced by the ₹20,000-crore net cash position and nearly nil debt. But investors should note contingent liabilities of ₹12,513 crore primarily from a disputed income-tax claim of ₹8,000 crore. The RHP mentions that these are not expected to have a material impact on financials.

MCL has strong profitability, which supports a high dividend yield of around 9 per cent. However, its growth has been lacklusture. It  will require volume and pricing growth to materialse, going forward.

title: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO: A dividend play
